summary: Iteration 20 backend-only verification of SEC-001 fix. 12/12 new SEC-001 tests PASS and 10/10 iter18 regression tests PASS (22/22 total). Verified: (1) POST /api/wipe/execute-complete returns HTTP 410 for the exact malicious payload {"confirmation":"COMPLETE_DEVICE_WIPE"}, for empty body, and for other variants; a canary vault item seeded before hitting the endpoint 3x is still present after, proving zero deletion. (2) POST /api/security/recovery/wipe returns 403 without valid wipe code, 400 without confirm:true, and 200 with wipe_code+confirm; device-scoping verified end-to-end (device A wiped -> A vault empty, B vault item intact). (3) Setup, verify-access (correct/wrong), telemetry+status (trust_score numeric 0-100, trap_level int), vault add/list/item/delete round-trip, family/create 6-char uppercase alnum code all still work. (4) CORS/general reachability confirmed via anonymous GET /api/security/status returning 200 JSON after allow_credentials was flipped True->False.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:1689 correctly raises HTTPException(410) with a helpful detail pointing callers to the owner-verified /api/security/recovery/wipe. The dangerous perform_complete_wipe() function has been removed from the module (grep confirms zero references remaining).

CORSMiddleware allow_credentials=False is consistent with the no-cookie/no-session single-device model. No client code sends cookies, so this is a safe hardening (mitigates CSRF risk for any future auth added).

security_engine.py recovery_wipe (line 1271) is correctly device-scoped: all delete_many calls filter by {device_id: req.device_id}, and device_state.update_one is also scoped by device_id. Verified empirically that wiping device A leaves device B's vault untouched.

Minor: recovery_wipe does not delete records from every collection that may hold device data (e.g. profiles/family_members/behavior_baselines are not enumerated). Not a security issue - just an inventory item for a future 'complete device data purge' feature.
test_credentials: Ephemeral per-run devices: TEST_sec001_A_<ts>, TEST_sec001_B_<ts>, TEST_sec001_canary_<ts>, TEST_sec001_base_<ts>. Codes: access=2580, recovery=rec999, wipe=wipe888.
seed_data_creation: All test devices are prefixed TEST_sec001_ and time-stamped; each test creates its own device and vault items. No shared/production data touched.
context_for_next_testing_agent: SEC-001 fix confirmed watertight. Reusable regression suite: /app/backend/tests/test_sec001_wipe_neutralized.py (12 tests, 13s) + /app/backend/tests/test_iter18_regression.py (10 tests, 7s). Run both after any change to server.py wipe endpoints, CORS config, or routes/security_engine.py recovery_wipe/_verify_wipe. Device-scoped wipe test uses vault items as canaries and is the most sensitive detector of any accidental cross-device deletion regression.
rca of the issue: N/A - fix already applied by main agent and verified working. Original SEC-001 was an unauthenticated global data-wipe (delete_many({}) on 12 shared collections) reachable by any anonymous caller at POST /api/wipe/execute-complete with a constant confirmation string. Mitigation: endpoint stubbed to raise 410 Gone; dangerous perform_complete_wipe() removed entirely; all wipes now flow through the bcrypt-gated, device-scoped /api/security/recovery/wipe.
